text: Disjunctivism about perception (Hinton, Snowdon, McDowell) is defined by its denial of:
choices: The existence of the external world
That hallucination can ever be subjectively indistinguishable from perception
The 'common factor' - a mental element shared by veridical perception and a matching hallucination
That veridical perception ever puts us in contact with objects
explanation: Disjunctivism denies the 'common factor' - the mental element supposedly shared by a veridical perception and a matching hallucination - holding instead that these are fundamentally different kinds of state. Option 0 is idealism, option 1 misstates the view (disjunctivists grant subjective indistinguishability), and option 3 is the reverse of their direct-realist commitment.
